sections.h2: Where is Bellevue, Nebraska, and how big has it grown?
sections.html:
Bellevue is a Sarpy County city that the Nebraska State Historical Society calls the state's oldest community, and it now has more than 64,000 residents. The Census Bureau counted 50,137 residents in 2010 and 64,176 in 2020.

The city also grew in area. The Census Bureau lists the city's land area at 15.85 square miles in 2010 and 21.13 square miles in 2020, with about 3,037 people per square mile in 2020. A house on the newer edge of town can therefore be in a very different neighborhood from one near the old center, even though both carry a Bellevue address.

The 2025 estimate of 64,863 is slightly below the 2020 census base of 65,059, so the Census Bureau's numbers show the city roughly level since the 2020 count.

Bellevue began around 1822 as a fur-trading post, and it later became the headquarters of a federal Indian agency. According to the State Historical Society's article Bellevue: The First Twenty Years, the post was set up by the Missouri Fur Company under Joshua Pilcher, then passed to Lucien Fontenelle and later to Peter A. Sarpy.

The agency for the Omaha, Pawnee, Oto and Missouri peoples moved to Bellevue in 1832. Missionaries and later Mormon, Oregon and California-bound travelers passed through, and the town came close to being chosen as the territorial capital.

sections.h2: What does Offutt Air Force Base mean for Bellevue home sellers?
sections.html:
Offutt Air Force Base, which MilitaryINSTALLATIONS ties to the Bellevue area, is the largest employer influence on the local economy. The same listing counts a combined military and civilian workforce of roughly 12,000 and more than 22,000 family members.

The base's own 2022 release described Offutt as Omaha's largest employer, with more than 6,000 military personnel and almost 4,000 civilians. It also says the 2019 flood destroyed about a third of the base, roughly $700 million of property, and that the rebuild of the southeastern portion was scheduled to wrap up around 2027.

Military households move on orders rather than on a seller's preferred timeline. A Bellevue owner who gets reassigned, inherits a house, or cannot rent it out may need a fast close that does not depend on a buyer's loan approval.

sections.h2: What does Bellevue's housing picture look like in Census data?
sections.html:
Bellevue is a majority owner-occupied city with a median owner-occupied home value of $247,000 in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey. The remaining 34.5 percent of occupied homes are not owner-occupied.

About 86.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which is typical of an established city and leaves a steady supply of long-held homes that may need updating before a traditional listing.

Bellevue Public Schools is the main district, and it describes itself as serving about 10,000 students. The district lists two high schools, three middle schools, 15 elementary schools, one alternative school and a career and technical education center for pre-kindergarten through grade 12.

It operates as part of Sarpy County and Educational Service Unit 3. Buyers with children will often ask which elementary and middle school a specific address feeds, so a seller should have the exact street address ready and confirm attendance areas with the district rather than guess.

sections.h2: What does Bellevue's housing code say about a house in poor condition?
sections.html:
Chapter 15 of the Bellevue Code of Ordinances gives the Permits and Inspections Department authority to inspect dwellings and to placard a dwelling as unfit for human habitation. A seller with a damaged or neglected property should know that process, because it affects both value and timing.

  • Section 15-21 lets the department enter and inspect dwellings at reasonable times, and owners or occupants must give access.
  • Section 15-24 gives a person who receives a notice ten days to file a written petition for a hearing. Without a petition the notice automatically becomes an order.
  • Section 15-29 lists the defects that support an unfit placard, including a dwelling that is dilapidated, unsanitary, difficult to heat, unsafe or vermin infested.
  • Section 15-34 bars a placarded home from being lived in again until the department removes the placard in writing.
  • Section 15-36 prohibits gas or electric service to a placarded dwelling except for authorized repairs.
  • Section 15-37 creates a five-member Board of Housing Appeals to hear appeals from department decisions.

The city's Code Enforcement Unit enforces city codes and zoning ordinances in Bellevue and its zoning jurisdiction. Under section 15-35, tenants of a placarded building owe no rent from the date the placard goes up, so an owner with renters should move quickly on any notice.

sections.h2: How do Sarpy County valuation and tax offices affect a Bellevue sale?
sections.html:
Bellevue property tax is billed by Sarpy County, so the county's Treasurer, Assessor and Clerk, not city hall, are the offices a seller deals with. The Sarpy County Treasurer's Office is in the 1102 Building at 1102 E. 1st Street in Papillion and warns that wait times peak between 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m., all day Fridays, and on the first and last day of any month.

The 2026 valuation protest period ran June 1 through June 30. Owners whose value changed received a goldenrod yellow postcard. A protest used Form 422 filed with the County Clerk at 1210 Golden Gate Drive in Papillion, in person by 4:45 p.m. on June 30, online by 11:59 p.m., or by mail postmarked by June 30. The county also cautions that a postal drop-box does not guarantee a same-day postmark, so mail should be postmarked in person at a post office.

Sarpy County's notice for 2025 gave the same June 1 through June 30 window, so a seller who thinks a value is too high before listing should plan for the June window rather than the closing date.

sections.h2: What does a Bellevue seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
A Bellevue seller pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax on the deed, set by section 76-901 at $3.32 per $1,000 of value for transfers before January 1, 2032. On a $247,000 sale, the figure shown by Census for a median-value home, that tax would be $820.04 (247 thousands at $3.32).

Nebraska law also requires a written condition statement from sellers of one-to-four-unit homes under section 76-2,120, covering appliances, electrical, heating and cooling, water, sewer, hazardous conditions and title issues such as easements. The seller has to update it before the buyer is bound if something changes.

  • Gather a payoff letter for any mortgage or lien.
  • Ask the title company how the current year's property tax will be split.
  • Pull the written condition statement together before any buyer asks.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with when selling a house in Bellevue?
faqs.a: Sarpy County. Bellevue property tax is billed and collected by the Sarpy County Treasurer in Papillion, and valuation protests are filed with the Sarpy County Clerk.

faqs.q: Can the city of Bellevue condemn a house in bad shape?
faqs.a: Yes, through a defined process. Under Chapter 15 of the city code, the Permits and Inspections Department can placard a dwelling as unfit, serve a notice of intent to condemn, and report to the city council. An owner can petition for a hearing within ten days of a notice.

faqs.q: How much is Nebraska deed stamp tax on a Bellevue sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000, for transfers before January 1, 2032. A $200,000 sale would owe $664.

faqs.q: When is the property valuation protest deadline in Sarpy County?
faqs.a: The protest period runs June 1 through June 30 each year. Form 422 goes to the Sarpy County Clerk, in person by 4:45 p.m. on June 30, online by 11:59 p.m., or by mail postmarked on or before June 30.

faqs.q: Does the Offutt base affect how fast Bellevue homes sell?
faqs.a: It shapes the buyer and seller pool, since the base employs roughly 12,000 people according to MilitaryINSTALLATIONS. This page does not state a sale speed, because no official source publishes one for Bellevue.
